html:
The Latvian Riflemen were units of the Russian army formed in 1915 from Latvian volunteers to defend Riga against the Germans in the First World War.

They fought hard and lost many men, notably in the Christmas Battles of 1916. In 1917 most of them sided with the Bolsheviks. The Red Latvian Riflemen guarded Lenin and the Kremlin, put down uprisings and fought through the Russian Civil War.

Other Latvians fought for an independent Latvia in the War of Independence. Many Red riflemen who stayed in the Soviet Union were killed in Stalin's purges of the 1930s. Their story shows how the First World War split the Latvian nation.
sum: The Latvian Riflemen were units of the Russian army formed in 1915 from Latvian volunteers to defend Riga against the Germans in the First World War.
